phase3_design_spine.spine_rationale: MOD-001 is the course motivational hook. Industry examples (Waymo, Boston Dynamics, Amazon Robotics) ARE the content, not a framing device. No failure-based spine is pedagogically appropriate here; the module functions as the answer to 'why does this course matter?'

design_problem.problem_statement: No engineering design problem is posed in this module. Instead, students are confronted with a market question: autonomous mobile robots are being deployed at scale across seven industry verticals — why now, and what does it take to build one? Every concept introduced in subsequent modules traces back to the real systems surveyed here.
design_problem.real_world_context: Global mobile robotics market projected at $215 billion by 2030 (CAGR ~26%). Waymo, Boston Dynamics, Amazon Robotics, Locus Robotics, and DJI represent the five dominant deployment profiles. Each maps to a different engineering challenge that this course resolves.

S005.note: S005 is the entirety of this module — the autonomy stack survey IS the design spine narrative.

industry_anchors.module_connection: Introduces full autonomy stack: perception → localization → planning → control. Sets the architectural template for the entire course.
Demonstrates differential drive at scale — connects to MOD-002 locomotion and MOD-008 navigation.
Legged locomotion morphology — connects to MOD-002 S001/S002.
Last-mile SLAM + local avoidance — connects to MOD-008 and MOD-009.
GPS-denied perception and precision navigation — connects to MOD-004 and MOD-005.
